summary: Both of my earlier minors are fixed, there are no new findings, and I approve this SHA. Minor 1: UserOutbox.enqueue now checks what update() returns. When no row is inserted it logs at WARN 'USER_DELETED outbox row already exists, duplicate suppressed: userId={}', with only the UUID and no email or other PII. UserOutboxIT checks that the WARN line appears only on the second enqueue and that it contains no '@example.com'. ADR 0011 at c:\Users\Akash\Desktop\Projects\.openforge\knowledge\decisions\0011-user-service-outbox.md, line 49, now records the assumption: one event per userId is correct only while auth-service disables deleted accounts. Minor 2: UserOutboxRelay.describe() now stores the root-cause class name and, if there is one, the root-cause message, cut to 500 characters. describeUsesRootCause tests both the root-cause text and the cut. The leftover risk of a broker host:port appearing in last_error is the same small, optional point I raised before, not a new issue. The new corrupt-payload guard (a null payload or a missing userId) throws the constant text 'Corrupt outbox payload', so no payload content reaches logs or last_error, and such rows go DEAD without being sent to Kafka (emptyPayloadsAreCorrupt). On the admin status change, the class-level @PreAuthorize(hasRole('ADMIN')) on UserOutboxAdminController is unchanged and is checked before the method runs. So the new 400 (CodedException VALIDATION_FAILED) can only reach callers who are already ADMIN, and it leaks nothing about the data. The status value is uppercased with Locale.ROOT and checked against an exact allow-list of DEAD and PENDING, then bound as a parameter, so there is no injection path. Rejecting unknown values instead of quietly treating them as DEAD is stricter than before. On the cancel-during-blocker test: the production path in PrivacyService.complete()/erase() did not change in this delta. The guarded claim (UPDATE ... SET status='COMPLETED' WHERE user_id=:u AND status='SCHEDULED') returns 0 rows after a cancel that lands between assertNoBlockers and the transaction, so nothing is erased and no outbox row is written. The new IT confirms this: the request stays CANCELLED, profile and address rows are unchanged, and there are zero outbox rows. The test's mock only changes a test-seeded row and adds no production code path. The OutboxMigrationIT pattern is now stricter (word-boundary ALTER, DROP or TRUNCATE). The delta adds no secrets, no dependencies and no changes to SecurityConfig.
